title: Workspace record
description: One item synced from an external workspace: a conversation, a message, a set of project instructions, an attachment's metadata. This is the canonical model, and no vendor's own shape reaches it — a mapper turns an observation into this, so that the day a vendor reorganises its message graph the change stops at the mapper. A record says how it was acquired and at what support level, because a record that does not cannot be told apart from a guess. Records live under .ai/local/workspaces/<workspace>/, are this checkout's state, and are never a source (ADR 0005, ADR 0025).

schema.description: The format version of this record. A version the tool does not know is refused, never guessed.

workspace.description: The id of the workspace declaration this record was synced under, `.ai/repo/workspaces/<id>.yaml`. A record whose declaration is gone is orphaned, not owned by whatever else is nearby.

vendor.description: The vendor id from the declaration, repeated here so a record read on its own still says who holds the original.

id.description: The local identity, `<vendor>:<type>:<upstream_id>`. Derived from the vendor and the upstream identifier and never from a title: a conversation renamed upstream is the same conversation, and two conversations may share a title on the same day.

upstream_id.description: The vendor's own identifier, carried opaquely and never parsed for meaning. Where the vendor gives none, a record is not invented — it is not synced.

type.description: What this record is. The set is closed: a shape the mapper cannot place is reported, not filed under whatever is closest.

transport.description: What carried this record. `official` is a documented, supported interface. `browser` is an authenticated browser session the operator already holds. `private_http` is an undocumented endpoint observed through that session — never one taken from a prompt, a gist or documentation.

acquisition.description: How this record arrived. Polling is not a subscription, and a record that says `poll` may not be presented as one that says `stream`.

support.description: How far this record may be trusted. `official` is a supported contract. `browser_observed` is what a rendered page showed. `private` came from an undocumented endpoint and may change without notice. `derived` was computed here from other records and is no stronger than its inputs.

contract.description: The observed contract this record was parsed under, where one applies: the fingerprint of the shape and the compatibility state at the time of parsing. Absent for `official`.

fingerprint.description: A hash of the observed shape, so that a vendor changing it is a diagnosable event rather than a silent wrong answer.

state.description: compatible: the shape matched. degraded: it did not, and no partial parse was persisted. incompatible: the mapper refuses this shape entirely.

parents.description: The local ids this record hangs from: a message's parent message, a conversation's project. A branching message graph is kept as a graph — flattening it to a list loses which answer replied to which question, and nothing downstream can recover it.

title.description: The vendor's display name for this item, carried for a listing and never used as an identity.

content_hash.description: A hash over the normalised body, so a re-sync that changed nothing writes a byte-identical record and a diff of the store means something.

body.description: The normalised content. Its shape follows `type`, and content parts keep their own type rather than being concatenated into a string. Absent where the declaration does not authorise reading the content, in which case the record is metadata only.

first_seen.description: When this record was first written here, RFC 3339 UTC. Not the vendor's creation time, which belongs in the body: this is a fact about the sync.

last_seen.description: When a sync last observed this record upstream, RFC 3339 UTC. A record whose last_seen falls behind the run that should have seen it is a candidate for a tombstone, never a silent deletion.

tombstone.description: Set when the record is gone upstream. The record stays: a corpus that deletes is a corpus that cannot say what it used to hold, and a vendor's outage is indistinguishable from a deletion unless the difference is written down.

reason.description: gone: the vendor no longer lists it. withdrawn: the declaration no longer authorises it. unreadable: it is listed and cannot be parsed.
